page: Microsoft Azure E160ads_v7 is a dedicated memory-optimized server configuration designed to run memory-intensive, latency-sensitive enterprise software. Built upon the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system is powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors clocked up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration delivers 160 dedicated virtual cores across 80 physical execution cores with simultaneous multithreading, coupled with a generous 1280 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Architectural features include 32 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES and SHA acceleration, as well as AVX-512 vector support including VNNI and BF16 execution units.

Storage architecture centers on an integrated 9449 GB local NVMe SSD array, offering substantial high-throughput temporary storage alongside the main memory footprint. The instance does not include GPU hardware accelerators, focusing strictly on high-density CPU and RAM processing. Benchmark evaluations position the system in the top tier of raw computing and memory performance. In multi-threaded evaluation, the platform achieved a stress-ng score of 287659.31 and a PassMark CPU score of 144267.77. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth reached 462.59 GB/sec for reads and 210.18 GB/sec for writes, validating high continuous data ingestion and memory access rates.

Application-level benchmarks demonstrate strong proficiency in data handling and network-adjacent execution, achieving over 202 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark database operations metric of 41416.44, and static web serving throughput of 109.88 GB/sec. On CPU-based inference workloads, small language models reached 5810.89 prompt processing tokens per second, while 7B parameter models recorded 371.42 tokens per second for prompt processing. While the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration limits training suitability for large deep learning models, its consolidated CPU compute density and multi-terabyte memory space reduce network-bound clustering overhead, making it cost-efficient for heavy in-memory database deployments, real-time analytics, and large-scale ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E160ads_v7 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for massive scale enterprise applications. Driven by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors running at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, this instance provisions 160 dedicated vCPUs across 80 physical cores alongside 1280 GB of memory. It features 9449 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPU acceleration. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance yields top-decile multi-core compute capability, exceeding 287,000 in stress-ng multi-core testing, complemented by large-block memory read bandwidth of 462.59 GB/sec. The integration of expansive memory capacity, rapid local disk I/O, and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 enables exceptional operational throughput, registering over 202 million Redis SET operations per second and robust database performance scores. By consolidating vast RAM pools and high-capacity scratch storage onto a single dedicated node, it maximizes operational efficiency for memory-heavy databases, real-time analytics engines, distributed caching clusters, and extensive data processing pipelines.
